knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

ASSIGNMENT:

1. Explain the difference between git add and git commit in your own words. Why are both steps necessary?
git add is responsible for moving the changes in the file in staging phase, while git commit saves that changes and make them permanent in your file. Both are necessary because it gives the author the control in reviewing the changes made before making it permanent.

2. A classmate says: 'If I delete a committed file from GitHub, my local copy will also be deleted.' Is this correct? What command would update the local copy?
Answer: No, because Github operates separately from the local repository. Using git pull, Github will fetch the latest commit in your history and merge it to an active branch.
